chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Harry White's club closes; Dave Nelson, King Oliver's nephew
summary: When the money got slick Harry White closed, and Dave Nelson, writer of Mule Face Blues, took over rehearsing the band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Then we closed the joint. Harry White closed because the money was slick. And Dave Nelson, who had been rehearsing, he...
Yeah, he's the one, King Oliver's nephew, Dave Nelson...
He wrote the "Mule Face Blues" and some other things. He was a good arranger. He was out of Chicago. And he and Jones, Richard M. Jones...
He wrote a lot of songs.
He used to live right across the hall from me in Chicago.
You told me that. He was a nice, nice gentleman.
Yeah, he wound up with one leg. Did you ever ...(?)...?
I don't know, maybe diabetes or one of them things. But he was a nice fellow.
He sure was a nice man.
